SWOG S0421 found that adding atrasentan to docetaxel and prednisone did not improve either co-primary progression-free or overall survival endpoint in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.
DAYBREAK-ALZ was terminated after independent assessment judged it unlikely to meet its primary endpoint upon completion; this is interim futility rather than a completed endpoint analysis.
NCT00773344 completed and has no posted results; no trial failure or discontinuation reason is inferred.

Across STARSHINE STARBEAM and STARBRIGHT idalopirdine added to cholinesterase inhibitors did not significantly improve week-24 ADAS-Cog cognition versus placebo.
Pooled PROTECT-1 and PROTECT-2 phase 3 analysis found no significant benefit on the prespecified primary clinical outcome with rolofylline versus placebo; both protocols completed.
METLung completed but onartuzumab plus erlotinib did not improve the primary overall-survival endpoint versus placebo plus erlotinib in MET-positive non-small-cell lung cancer.

MERU was stopped after prespecified futility for overall survival in DLL3-high small-cell lung cancer; median overall survival was 8.5 versus 9.8 months for Rova-T and placebo. Investigator-assessed progression-free survival improved but planned central assessment was not performed.
TAHOE completed with inferior overall survival on Rova-T versus topotecan (median 6.3 versus 8.6 months; hazard ratio 1.46).
Primary efficacy outcome did not support continued development; verify exact program-level wording.

Published BRISK-PS phase 3 trial NCT00825955 found no statistically significant overall-survival improvement with brivanib versus placebo plus best supportive care after sorafenib failure or intolerance.
The separate Asia-Pacific BRISK-APS study is marked terminated but its registry does not state a reason; the BRISK-PS endpoint result must not be copied to this protocol.

Bristol Myers Squibb disclosed that it terminated the broader brivanib development program during 2012. The filing does not identify a protocol-specific stopping cause for BRISK-APS or establish an independent BRISK-APS endpoint failure.

LIGHT phase 3 (n=1035) did not meet its prespecified overall-survival superiority or noninferiority criteria versus sorafenib (median 9.1 vs 9.8 months; HR 1.046, 95% CI 0.896-1.221). Time to progression and response rate favored linifanib, but serious and grade 3/4 adverse events were more frequent. The registry records IDMC-recommended discontinuation without a more specific stated stopping rationale; this event describes the published endpoint result, not an inferred stopping cause.

The safety-focused extension enrolled patients continuing motesanib from other trials and was terminated by Amgen decision. The registry gives no protocol-specific efficacy or safety cause; MONET1's outcome is not assigned to this extension.

MONET1's amended nonsquamous NSCLC population (n=1090) did not have significantly improved overall survival with motesanib plus carboplatin/paclitaxel versus chemotherapy alone (median 13.0 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.90; p=0.14). PFS and response rate favored motesanib, while severe adverse events were more frequent. The registry states that Amgen discontinued development because the study missed its primary objective.

Within the same MONET1 protocol, squamous-histology enrollment and treatment stopped after higher early mortality and gross hemoptysis with motesanib. The squamous-cohort publication reports 23/182 versus 10/178 fatal adverse events within 60 days and six versus zero fatal bleeding events. This is a cohort-specific safety event, not a separate trial or the nonsquamous efficacy endpoint.

Gilead states it terminated the multi-cohort phase 2 study after deciding to discontinue its entospletinib development; the registry does not state that a prespecified efficacy endpoint failed. Published CLL cohorts reported clinical activity.

Kronos Bio terminated AGILITY enrollment before its planned sample because recruiting fit participants with NPM1-mutated AML was difficult and post-COVID constraints persisted; this is not a reported primary efficacy-endpoint failure.
UNITE ocular-side-effect prophylaxis enrollment stopped after the separate INTELLANCE-1 survival analysis showed no benefit; UNITE did not itself test or fail a survival primary endpoint.

The phase 1 dose-finding portion reported modest activity and a recommended phase 2 dose; the planned phase 2 portion was not undertaken because the company discontinued development for this indication. The registry labels the protocol terminated for that company decision.
NCT02730884 terminated at investigator request due to low accrual; three participants enrolled. This does not imply efficacy failure.
NCT01055067 stopped for futility under its Simon two-stage rule after no complete or partial responses in stage one.

The planned phase 3 study was withdrawn before enrollment (0 participants). The sponsor attributed cancellation to results of a different study with a similar hypothesis and agent; no efficacy endpoint was tested in NCT01266811.
Completed phase 2 saracatinib monotherapy study reported no qualifying PSA responses among 28 patients; its prespecified PSA response signal was not observed.

The later randomized-discontinuation study ended under its lead-in futility rule because only eight of 31 treated patients remained stable enough for randomization. The planned randomized comparison was therefore not adequately tested; this is not an observed failure of that primary comparison.

aV1ation pediatric phase 2 did not improve the prespecified Vineland-II two-domain composite at week 24 versus placebo (primary-analysis treatment difference -0.16; p=0.91). Registry stopping text reports no clinical or statistical primary-endpoint benefit and no new safety concern.
STABILITY and SOLID-TIMI 52 completed without meeting their respective primary cardiovascular outcomes; the separate Mayo endothelial-function trial was also negative.

The NSCLC trial registry states that the pharmaceutical company discontinued the study drug; the published trial reported a 22% objective response rate and does not support labeling the protocol an efficacy-endpoint failure.
The global phase 3 study stopped after Myriad discontinued Flurizan development following the separate U.S. phase 3 failure; its own co-primary endpoints are not reported as failed.
The completed U.S. Act-Earli-AD phase 3 trial found no statistically significant benefit on either co-primary outcome: ADAS-Cog cognition or ADCS-ADL function.
The open-label safety extension stopped after Flurizan development was discontinued following the separate U.S. efficacy trial; it did not fail an efficacy primary endpoint.

V1aduct adult phase 3 stopped after an interim futility analysis found the predefined primary Vineland-II two-domain objective highly unlikely to be met. The interim treatment difference was -1.84 (95% CI -5.15 to 1.48); no new safety concern was identified. This is the randomized efficacy trial, not an independent extension failure.

VANILLA phase 2 in adult men did not improve its prespecified Social Responsiveness Scale-2 primary endpoint at week 12 versus placebo. The same publication reported a favorable dose-dependent secondary Vineland-II adaptive-behavior signal; that secondary finding does not turn the primary endpoint into a success.
Registry states the mesothelioma study ended when the sponsor terminated its study agreement; the underlying agreement rationale and whether an efficacy endpoint failed are not established.
Extension publication reports that parent Phase 3 protocols were stopped early for lack of efficacy.
CREAD 2 was discontinued after an interim analysis in the separate CREAD study indicated crenezumab was unlikely to meet its primary endpoint; CREAD 2 did not reach its own week 105 primary endpoint.

The manufacturer decided not to pursue additional brivanib research in metastatic renal cell carcinoma and requested closure to accrual. The registry reports unavailable outcome data after the investigator left; no primary efficacy-endpoint failure was established.
INTELLANCE-1 found no overall-survival benefit at its prespecified interim analysis and stopped early for futility; the reported PFS difference did not establish an OS benefit.

TRINOVA-2 did not improve its primary PFS endpoint (median 7.6 versus 7.2 months); ORR and duration of response improved. Enrollment was truncated after a PLD shortage; later registry termination described long-term follow-up closure, not the cause of the PFS result.

TRINOVA-3 did not improve primary PFS in first-line advanced ovarian cancer (15.9 versus 15.0 months; HR 0.93; p=0.36). Later administrative long-term follow-up closure should not be described as efficacy-driven trial termination.

No failure event is assigned to TRINOVA-1: its primary PFS endpoint was met (7.2 versus 5.4 months; HR 0.66; p<0.0001). This positive trial must not be collapsed into the negative TRINOVA-2/3 results.

Published phase I/IIa pilot (n=30) reported generally tolerable treatment; six active-treatment patients had moderate asymptomatic reversible transaminase elevations. Secondary cognitive trends were not statistically significant in this small trial. No stopping or efficacy-failure reason is assigned to this safety-focused study; the later ARGO efficacy result is a separate event.
The ARGO phase 2 publication reported no statistically significant clinical efficacy benefit in Alzheimer disease.

The IMPACTS-2 sickle-cell study terminated after enrolling two participants because of a registry-stated change in company plans; neither efficacy failure nor a specific connection to VISTA-16 is established.

The completed PLASMA study found a significant dose-dependent reduction in week-8 secretory phospholipase A2 group IIA concentration versus placebo. This surrogate biomarker response did not establish prevention of cardiovascular events.

The completed FRANCIS-ACS study met its week-8 LDL-cholesterol biomarker endpoint with varespladib plus atorvastatin versus placebo plus atorvastatin; secretory phospholipase A2 group IIA also fell. This phase 2 biomarker signal did not establish fewer major cardiovascular events.
Primary publication reported no improvement in coronary endothelial function in the registered trial.
The completed REACH CDM trial did not reach conventional significance on its registered primary CDM1-RS endpoint (p=0.0514); this does not establish discontinuation of the development program.
GRADUATE I did not meet its primary CDR-SB clinical endpoint; the registry lists the trial as terminated.
GRADUATE II did not meet its primary CDR-SB clinical endpoint; the registry lists the trial as terminated.
DSMB recommended discontinuation for an unfavorable benefit-risk balance; registry cites no evidence of potential efficacy and an adverse-event profile worse than placebo.
DSMB recommended discontinuation for an unfavorable benefit-risk balance; registry cites no evidence of potential efficacy and an adverse-event profile worse than placebo.

EARLY phase 2b/3 dosing and enrollment stopped after dose-related liver-enzyme elevations in atabecestat recipients changed the sponsor's benefit-risk assessment; subsequent cognitive analyses were not the original stopping trigger.
The phase 2 long-term extension was terminated as part of the atabecestat program stop after liver-enzyme elevations; this is not a separate failed efficacy endpoint.

LUSTER-1 completed but did not show a statistically significant reduction in moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations after multiplicity adjustment; program development in asthma was then stopped after pooled LUSTER review.
LUSTER-2 completed but did not show a statistically significant reduction in moderate-to-severe asthma exacerbations after multiplicity adjustment; a numerical reduction does not establish success.
ZEAL-1 completed but did not meet the primary pre-dose FEV1 improvement endpoint at week 12; adjusted p=0.088 in the primary publication.
ZEAL-2 completed but did not meet the primary pre-dose FEV1 improvement endpoint at week 12; adjusted p=0.214 in the primary publication.
CHROMA phase 3 primary week-48 analysis found no reduction in geographic atrophy lesion enlargement with lampalizumab versus sham.
SPECTRI phase 3 primary week-48 analysis found no reduction in geographic atrophy lesion enlargement with lampalizumab versus sham; one regimen had a numerically worse lesion-area change.

Pfizer and Lilly discontinued global tanezumab development after an FDA Complete Response Letter for osteoarthritis and a negative EMA CHMP opinion. Joint safety concerns featured in regulatory review; representative phase 3 trials had efficacy signals and are not classified as endpoint failures.
EMBODY 1 completed but epratuzumab plus standard therapy did not significantly improve week-48 BICLA response versus placebo plus standard therapy.
EMBODY 2 completed but epratuzumab plus standard therapy did not significantly improve week-48 BICLA response versus placebo plus standard therapy.

Janssen reported an FDA Complete Response Letter for the RA BLA requesting additional clinical data to evaluate safety. The completed SIRROUND trials had efficacy signals and are not classified as endpoint failures.
Janssen withdrew the EMA marketing authorization application for RA; EMA reported outstanding concerns and the company cited the need for additional clinical data and portfolio prioritization.
SYNERGY missed its primary multicomponent endpoint for confirmed disability improvement; this event did not end development because AFFINITY followed.
AFFINITY Part 1 missed its primary and key secondary endpoints; the subsequent Part 2 termination was explicitly not attributed to safety concerns.
Biogen discontinued opicinumab development after the negative AFFINITY phase 2 results; this program decision is distinct from the SYNERGY and AFFINITY trial endpoint events.
SPARK showed no meaningful difference in MDS-UPDRS progression or DaT-SPECT imaging versus placebo; the trial stopped for lack of efficacy after interim analysis.
Biogen discontinued cinpanemab development after SPARK missed its primary and secondary endpoints; this is a separate program decision from the trial outcome.
PASSPORT showed no statistically significant improvement in week-52 PSP Rating Scale score versus placebo; key clinical secondary endpoints also lacked efficacy.
Biogen discontinued gosuranemab development for PSP and other primary tauopathies after PASSPORT while explicitly continuing the separate Alzheimer disease TANGO study.
GAMMA-1 completed without an overall-survival benefit from adding andecaliximab to mFOLFOX6 versus placebo plus mFOLFOX6; a higher response rate did not establish primary-endpoint success.

TANGO did not meet the prespecified week-78 CDR-SB efficacy endpoint and its extension was stopped for lack of efficacy; the protocol-listed primary outcomes were safety and tolerability and are not described as failed.
The PSP study met prespecified interim futility criteria and showed no significant week-52 PSP Rating Scale benefit with tilavonemab versus placebo.
RAINIER was terminated after its second interim analysis met prespecified futility criteria; simtuzumab did not improve progression-free survival in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
MINDSET completed but intepirdine plus donepezil did not significantly improve either co-primary week-24 ADAS-Cog cognition or ADCS-ADL function versus placebo plus donepezil.
APECS was terminated on a prespecified futility recommendation; verubecestat showed no benefit versus placebo on its CDR-SB primary clinical outcome in prodromal Alzheimer disease.
STABILITY completed but darapladib did not significantly reduce its primary cardiovascular death myocardial infarction or stroke composite versus placebo.
SOLID-TIMI 52 completed but darapladib did not significantly reduce its primary major coronary events composite after acute coronary syndrome.

VISTA-16 was stopped after prespecified interim review for futility and possible harm. The primary composite was not significantly improved and myocardial infarction risk was higher with varespladib than placebo; this is not a failure of the unrelated PLA2G7 target.
